column1: # Syllabic shorthand: one or two letters per syllable, chosen on the spot.
# Nobody is following a system here.  The same word gets different letters on
# different days -- "stratification" is satfcatn one time and stfcatn the next
# -- so what these cases test is not a codebook but the claim in
# spellless/cue.lua: that the letters a person *drops* are predictable even
# when the ones they keep are not.
# Rank 5 rather than 1 for most of them.  These inputs are genuinely lossy and
# several readings usually survive; what matters is that the word is on the
# first page at all, which before spellless/cue.lua it very often was not.
# Long technical words, where shorthand pays for itself most
# Everyday words.  These have far more competition: half the dictionary is a
# plausible reading of five letters out of "development".
# Short input, where the shorthand reading has to fight a dictionary full of
# short words that fit it exactly.  "tnk" really is the skeleton of "tank";
# that it should still offer "think" is a claim about frequency, not spelling.
